1.1: To Know Wisdom The Proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, Who reigned in Israel,
1.2: To know wisdom and instruction, And to understand words of discernment;
1.3: To receive both subtlety of words, And to understand true righteousness and upright judgment;
1.4: So as to give astuteness to the simple, And both perception and understanding to a young man;
1.5: For a wise man who hears these things will be wiser, And the man of understanding will gain direction. Wisdom Begets the Fear of God
1.6: He will understand both a parable and a hidden say ing, Both wise words and riddles.
1.7: The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, And there is good understanding in all who practice it;
1.8: And godliness toward God is the beginning of perception, But the ungodly despise wisdom and instruction.
1.9: Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, And do not reject the laws of your mother.
1.10: For you will receive a crown of grace on your head And a gold chain around your neck.
1.11: My son, do not let the ungodly lead you astray, And do not consent if they invite you, saying,
1.12: “Com e with us; take part in bloodshed, And let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
1.13: And let us swallow him, just as Hades does the living, And let us take away his remembrance from the earth;
1.14: Let us seize his valuable property, And let us fill our houses with spoils;
1.15: Cast your lot with us And let us acquire a common bag; Let there be one purse for us.”
1.16: Do not walk in the way with them, But turn away your foot from their paths.
1.17: For their feet run to evil, And they make haste to shed blood.
1.18: For nets are not spread before birds for no reason, For those who participate in murder store up evils for themselves; And evil is the destruction of lawless men.
1.19: These are the ways of all who accomplish lawless things, For they take away their own soul in ungodliness. Wisdom Speaks Out
1.20: Wisdom sings in the streets; She moves boldly in the squares.
1.21: She preaches on high city walls And sits at the gates of lords. At the gates of a city she boldly says,
1.22: “So long a time as the simple hold fast to righteousness, They shall not be ashamed;
1.23: But those without discernment, since they are desirous of arrogance, And are become ungodly, they hate perception, And are become subject to reproofs.
1.24: Behold, I shall bring forth upon you the utterance of my breath, And I shall teach you my word.
1.25: Since I called, but you did not obey, And spoke at length, but you paid no attention,
1.26: But made my counsels invalid, And were not persuaded by my reproofs;
1.27: Consequently, I will laugh at your annihilation, And will exult when ruin comes to you,
1.28: And when confusion reaches you unawares, And overthrow comes like a whirlwind,
1.29: And when tribulation and anguish come to you, And when destruction comes to you.
1.30: For it shall be, when you shall call upon me, I will not listen to you;
1.31: Evil men will seek me, but not find me, For they hate wisdom, and choose not the fear of the Lord.
1.32: Neither do they wish to follow my counsels, But despise my reproofs.
1.33: Therefore, they shall eat the fruits of their own way And be filled with their own ungodliness.
1.34: For since they wrong the simple, they shall be killed, And a close examination shall destroy the ungodly.
1.35: But he who obeys me shall dwell in hope, And shall be at rest without fear from every evil.”

2.1: It Is Wise to Obey My son, if you receive the words of my commandment And hide them within yourself,
2.2: Your ear will be obedient to wisdom, And you will incline your heart to understanding; You will entrust it to your son as an admonition.
2.3: For if he calls upon wisdom, And you utter your voice for understanding; If you seek perception with a strong voice,
2.4: If you seek her as silver And search for her as treasure,
2.5: Then you will understand the fear of the Lord And find the knowledge of God.
2.6: For the Lord gives wisdom, And from His face come knowledge and understanding;
2.7: And He stores up salvation for the upright; He will protect their journey,
2.8: That He might guard the ways of His ordinances; And He will carefully guard the way of those who reverence Him.
2.9: Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, And accomplish successfullyeverygood path for yourself. Holy Thinking
2.10: For if wisdom comes into your mind, And the perception in your soul seems to be good,
2.11: Then good counsel will guard you, And holy thinking will keep you;
2.12: That it might rescue you from an evil way And froma man who speaks nothing trustworthy.
2.13: Woe to those who forsake the paths of uprightness So they may walk in the ways of darkness,
2.14: Who delight in evils And rejoice in evil perversion,
2.15: Whose ways are crooked And their paths devious,
2.16: So they may cause you to be far from the straight way And a stranger to righteous judgment.
2.17: My son, do not lay hold of evil counsel, Nor forsake the teaching of your youth And forget the divine covenant;
2.18: For it establishes its house with death, And its paths beside Hades with the dead;
2.19: All who journey there do not return, Nor do they lay hold of straight paths; For they do not comprehend the years of life.
2.20: For if they walked in good paths, They would find the smooth paths of righteousness.
2.21: The inhabitants of the land will be good, And the simple will be left in it;
2.22: For the upright will dwell in the land, And the holy will be left in it.
2.23: The ways of the ungodly shall perish from the land, And the lawless shall be banished from it.

3.1: My son, do not forget my laws, The Laws of Wisdom But let your heart keep my words;
3.2: For length of days, and years of life and peace They will add to you.
3.3: Do not let almsgiving and faithfulness forsake you, But hang them upon your neck;
3.4: And you will find grace And provide good things before the Lord and men.
3.5: Trust in God with all your heart, And do not exalt your own wisdom.
3.6: In all your ways know wisdom, That she may cut a straight path for you; And your foot will not stumble.
3.7: Do not relyon your own discernment, But fear God, and turn away from every evil.
3.8: Then there shall be healing for your body And care for your bones.
3.9: Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, And offer Him the firstfruits from the fruits of your righteousness,
3.10: That your storehouses may be filled with abundance of grain, And your winepresses maygush with wine. The Instruction of Wisdom
3.11: My son, do not despise the instruction of the Lord, Neither grow weary under His reproof.
3.12: For whom the Lord loves He instructs, And chastises every son He receives.
3.13: Blessed is a man who finds wisdom, And a mortal who sees discernment;
3.14: For the profits gained from wisdom are better Than the treasures of gold and silver.
3.15: And wisdom is more valuable than precious stones, And nothing evil will withstand her;
3.16: She is well known to all who come near her, And no honor is worthy of her.
3.17: For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, And in her left hand are riches and glory;
3.18: Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, And she carries law and mercy upon her tongue.
3.19: Her ways are good ways, And all her paths are in peace.
3.20: She is a tree of life for all who cleave to her, And she is security for those who lean upon her as upon the Lord.
3.21: God by wisdom founded the earth And prepared the heavens with discernment.
3.22: With perception the depths were broken up, And the clouds flowed with dew. The Cure for Carelessness
3.23: My son, do not be careless, But keep my counsel and thinking,
3.24: That your soul may live, And grace may be around your neck.
3.25: And there will be healing for your flesh And care for your bones,
3.26: That you may walk confidently in peace in all your ways, And your foot may not stumble.
3.27: For if you sit down, you will be without fear, And if you lie down, your sleep will be pleasant.
3.28: And do not be afraid of in tim id ation when it comes upon you, Nor of the attack of the ungodly when it comes at you;
3.29: For the Lord will be over all your ways, And He will plant your feet firm ly, that you may not be shaken.
3.30: Do not withhold doing good to the needy, When you may give a helping hand;
3.31: Do not say, when you are able to do good, “Com e back tomorrow, and I will give you something”; For you do not know what the next day will bring forth.
3.32: Do not devise evil things against your friend Who dwells beside you and trusts in you.
3.33: Do not be ready to quarrel with a man in vain, Lest he do you some harm.
3.34: Do not incur the reproach of evil men, Neither seek their way s;
3.35: For every lawless man is unclean before the Lord, And he does not sit am ong the righteous.
3.36: The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly, But He blesses the dwellings of the righteous.
3.37: The Lord opposes the arrogant, But He gives grace to the humble.
3.38: The wise shall inherit glory, But the ungodly exalt dishonor.

4.1: Obedient Thinking Hear, my children, the instruction of your father, And pay attention, that you might know his thinking;
4.2: For I offer a good gift to you; Do not forsake my law.
4.3: For I was a son, and I was obedient to my father, And beloved in the presence of my mother,
4.4: Who taught me, saying, “Let our word become firm ly planted in your heart;
4.5: Guard our commandments; do not forget them; Neither disregard the word of my mouth,
4.6: Nor forsake it, and it shall cleave to you; Love it, and it will keep you.
4.7: Secure it, and it shall exalt you; Honor it, that it may embrace you,
4.8: And give your head a crown of graces, And cover you with a crown of delight.” The Paths of Wisdom
4.9: Hear me, my son, and receive my words, And the years of your life shall be increased, That many ways of life may be yours;
4.10: For I teach you the ways of wisdom And set you on upright paths.
4.11: For if you walk, your steps shall not be confined; And if you run, you will not grow weary.
4.12: Lay hold of my instruction; do not let go, But guard it for yourself as your life.
4.13: Do not go in the ways of the ungodly, Neither be zealous for the ways of the lawless;
4.14: In whatever place they encamp, do not go there, But turn aside from them and pass by.
4.15: For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; Their sleep is taken away, and they do not rest;
4.16: For they feed on the bread of ungodliness, And they are drunk with the wine of lawlessness.
4.17: But the ways of the righteous shine like a light; They go before and give light until full daylight.
4.18: But the ways of the ungodly are dark; They do not know how they stumble. The Wise Heart
4.19: My son, give heed to my word And incline your ear to my words,
4.20: That your fountains may not fail you; Guard them in your heart;
4.21: For they are life to those who find them And healing for all their flesh.
4.22: Keep your heart with all watchfulness, For from these words are the issues of life.
4.23: Put away from yourself a crooked mouth And remove unrighteous lips far from you.
4.24: Let your eyes look straight forward, And let your eyelids assent to righteous things.
4.25: Make straight paths for your feet And direct your ways aright.
4.26: Do not turn aside to the right or to the left, But turn your foot from an evil way;
4.27: For God knows the way son the right hand, But those on the left are perverse;
4.28: And He shall make your paths straight And guide your steps in peace.

5.1: My son, hold fast to wisdom Fornication or Marriage And incline your ear to my words,
5.2: That you may guard good thinking; And I command you with the perception of my lips.
5.3: Do not join yourself to a base woman, For honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, Or for a season she is pleasing to your taste;
5.4: Afterward, however, you will find her more bitter than gall And sharper than a two-edged sword.
5.5: For feet lacking discernment lead those using her down into Hades with death; Her footsteps are not planted,
5.6: For she does not travel the ways of life; And her paths are slippery and not easy to discern. The Perils of Sex outside of Marriage
5.7: Now therefore, my son, hear me, And do not make my words invalid;
5.8: Make your way distant from her And do not come near the doors of her house,
5.9: That you may not give away your life to others And your existence to the m erciless;
5.10: That strangers may not be filled with your strength, And your labors go into the houses of strangers,
5.11: And you should feel regret at the last, When the flesh of your body is consumed;
5.12: And you will say, “How I hated instruction And turned my heart away from reproofs;
5.13: I did not hear the voice of my instructor and teacher, Nor did I incline my ear;
5.14: Little by little I was in every evil In the midst of the church and congregation.” The Sanctity of Marriage
5.15: Drink waters from your vessels And from the fountains of your spring.
5.16: Do not let the waters from your fountain be spilled by you, But let your waters pass through your wide places;
5.17: Let them be only for you, And let no stranger partake with you;
5.18: Let the fountain of your water be for you alone, And rejoice together with the wife of your youth.
5.19: Let your loving deer and graceful colt keep company with you, And let her alone go before you and be with you at all times; For in living with her love, you will be great. Another Warning
5.20: Do not be intimate with a strange woman, Neither cling to the embrace of a woman not your own;
5.21: For the ways of man are before the eyes of God, And He keeps close watch on all his paths.
5.22: Lawless women ensnare a man, But each man is bound by the chains of his own sins.
5.23: Such a man dies with the uninstructed And is cast forth from the abundance of his own substance; And he is destroyed by lack of discernment.

6.1: A Careless Tongue My son, if you assume the debt of your friend, You will deliver your hand to an enemy;
6.2: For a m an's own lips become a strong snare to him, And he is conquered by the utterances of his own mouth.
6.3: My son, do what I command you, and you will save yourself; For you came into the hands of evil things through your friend;
6.4: Do not be faint, But provoke even your friend, for whom you assumed a debt;
6.5: Do not give sleep to your eyes Nor slumber to your eyelids
6.6: That you may be saved, as a gazelle from the snares, And as a bird from a trap. Laziness: A Dead-End Road
6.7: Compare yourself with the ant, O sluggard, And be zealous when you see his ways, And become wiser than he.
6.8: For although he has no tilled land, Neither anyone to compel him, Nor any master to rule him,
6.9: Yet he prepares all his food in the summer And makes his provisions abundant in the winter.
6.10: Or go to the honey bee, And learn how she is a worker And howsolemnlyshe does her work,
6.11: Whose labors kings and common people use for health; And she is desirable to all and glorious;
6.12: And although she is weak in bodily strength, She leads the way in honoring wisdom.
6.13: How long, O sluggard, will you be idle, And when will you arise from sleep?
6.14: You sleep a little; you sit down a little; you doze a short while; And you fold your hands on your chest a little;
6.15: Then poverty comes to you as an evil traveler And neediness as a swift runner.
6.16: But if you are diligent, your harvest shall come to you as a fountain, And neediness as an evil runner shall desert you. A Lawless Spirit
6.17: A man who is without discernment and is lawless does not walk in good ways. But he winks with an eye; he makes a sign with his foot, And teaches with the wave of his hand.
6.18: And with a perverse heart, he constantly schemes evil things; Such a man causes trouble in a city.
6.19: Therefore his destruction comes suddenly, A deep and incurable wound.
6.20: For he rejoices in everything the Lord hates, And he shall be broken because of his soul's uncleanness:
6.21: A haughty eye, an unrighteous tongue, Hands that shed righteous blood,
6.22: A heart that devises evil thoughts, And feet that hasten to do evil;
6.23: As a false witness he kindles injustice And causes quarrels between brethren.
6.24: My son, guard the laws of your father, And do not depart from the rules of your mother.
6.25: But fasten them to your soul continually And wear them as a collar upon your neck. Playing with Fire
6.26: When you walk about, bring along this commandment And let it be with you;
6.27: And as you sleep, let it guard you, That when you arise, it may speak to you.
6.28: For a commandment of law is a lamp and a light, And the way of life is reproof and instruction,
6.29: That you may keep yourself froma married woman And from the slanderous tongue of a strange woman.
6.30: Do not let the desire of beauty conquer you; Neither be caught by her eyes, Nor captivated by her eyelids;
6.31: For the value of a prostitute is only one loaf, And such a woman hunts for the precious souls of men.
6.32: Shall any one bind fire to his bosom And his garments not burn?
6.33: Or will any one walk about on coals of fire And not burn his feet?
6.34: Likewise is the one who goes in to a married woman; He shall not be guiltless, nor any who touch her.
6.35: It is not surprising if any one who steals is caught, For he steals that he may fill his hungry soul;
6.36: But if he is caught, he will repay sevenfold, And by giving all his goods, he shall deliver himself.
6.37: But the adulterer through his lack of discernment Obtains the destruction of his soul;
6.38: He bears both pain and dishonor, And his disgrace will not be wiped away forever.
6.39: For the anger of her husband is full of jealousy; He will not spare in the day of judgment;
6.40: He will not take any ransom in exchange for his hatred, Nor will he be reconciled by many gifts.

7.1: My son, guard my words, A Son with Discernment And hide my commandments within yourself;
7.2: My son, honor the Lord, and you shall be strong, And fear none other but Him.
7.3: Guard my commandments And you will live, and my words as the pupils of your eyes;
7.4: And put them around your fingers, And write them upon the breadth of your heart.
7.5: Say that wisdom is your sister, And gain discernment as a friend for yourself,
7.6: So they may keep you froma strange and evil woman, If she comes at you with flattering words. A Son without Discernment
7.7: For she looks froma window of her house into the streets Upon whom she might see among the undiscerning children,
7.8: A young man lacking discernment Passing by near the corner on the pathways of her house;
7.9: And she speaks in the darkness at evening, When there is silence on a dark night;
7.10: And the woman meets him, having the appearance of a prostitute; She makes the heart of young men throb.
7.11: She is excited and debauched, And her feet do not rest at home.
7.12: For at times she is outside roaming about, And another time she is in the streets near every corner lay ing a trap.
7.13: Then lay ing hold of him, she kisses him, And with a sham eless face she says to him,
7.14: “I have a peace offering; Today I pay my vows;
7.15: For this reason I came out to meet you; Longing for your face, I found you;
7.16: I spread my bed with sheets And covered it with tapestry from Egypt.
7.17: I sprinkled my bed with saffron And my house with cinnamon;
7.18: Come, and let us enjoy love until morning; Come, and let us embrace in love;
7.19: For my husband is not at home, But is gone on a long journey
7.20: Taking a bag of money in his hand; He will return to his house after many days.”
7.21: So she leads him astray with much conversation, And with snares from her lips she compels him.
7.22: And being cajoled, he follows her As an ox is led for slaughter
7.23: And as a dog to bonds, Or as a deer struck with an arrow in the liver;
7.24: And he hastens even as a bird into a snare, Not knowing he runs for his life.
7.25: Now therefore, my son, hear me, And hold fast to the words of my mouth;
7.26: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways, For she wounded and cast down many, And those whom she slew are innumerable;
7.27: Her house is the road to Hades, Leading down to the chambers of death.

8.1: You shall proclaim wisdom Divine Wisdom for Mankind That discernment may obey you;
8.2: For she is on the lofty summit And stands in the midst of the paths.
8.3: For she sits beside the gates of princes And sings at the entrances,
8.4: “You, O men, I exhort, And I utter my voice to the sons of men;
8.5: Understand astuteness, O simple ones, And put it in your heart, O uninstructed ones.
8.6: Obey me, for I speak sacred things, And from my lips I will bring forth things that are true.
8.7: For my mouth shall speak the truth, But false lips are an abomination before me.
8.8: All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; There is nothing in them crooked or twisted.
8.9: All things are evident to those who understand And true to those who find knowledge.
8.10: Lay hold of instruction and not silver, And knowledge rather than tested gold, And choose perception rather than pure gold.
8.11: For wisdom is better than precious stones, And every costly thing is not worthy of her.
8.12: I, wisdom, dwell with counsel, And I call upon knowledge and understanding.
8.13: The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, And both rudeness and arrogance, and the ways of wicked men; And I hate the perverted ways of evil men.
8.14: Counsel and safety are mine; Discernment is mine, and strength is mine;
8.15: By me, kings reign, And princes write of righteousness;
8.16: By me, noblemen become great, And by me, monarchs have power in the land.
8.17: I love those who love me, And those who seek me shall find me.
8.18: Riches and glory belong to me, And abundant possessions, and righteousness;
8.19: It is better to enjoy my fruits than gold and precious stones, And my fruits are better than choice silver.
8.20: I walk in the ways of righteousness, And I amconversant with the paths of judgment;
8.21: That I maydistribute substance to those who love me, And may fill their treasuries with good things. Divine Wisdom and the Father
8.22: “If I declare to you the things that happen daily, I will also remember to recount the things of old.
8.23: The Lord created me in the beginning of His ways for His works; He established me in the beginning before time,
8.24: Before He made the earth, and before He made the abysses, Before the going forth of the fountains of waters,
8.25: Before the mountains were created; And He begot me before all hills.
8.26: The Lord made the fields and the uninhabited places And the inhabited heights under heaven.
8.27: When He prepared heaven, I was present with Him, And when He set apart His throne upon the winds.
8.28: When He made strong the things above the clouds, And made sure the fountains under heaven,
8.29: And made strong the foundations of the earth, I was working beside Him;
8.30: I was He in whom He rejoiced; Daily and continually I was gladdened by His face.
8.31: When He completed the world, He rejoiced, And He rejoiced in the sons of men.
8.32: Now therefore, my son, hear me: Blessed is the man who shall hearken to me And the man who shall guard my ways;
8.33: Who watches daily at my doors, Who keeps watch at the doors of my entry ways;
8.34: For my issues are the issues of life, And grace is prepared from the Lord.
8.35: But those who sin against me act ungodly toward their own souls, And those who hate me love death.”

9.1: Wisdom built her house, Wisdom's Invitation And she supported it with seven pillars.
9.2: She offered her sacrifices; She mixed her wine in a bowl And prepared her table.
9.3: She sent her servants, Inviting people to the bowl with a lofty proclamation, saying,
9.4: “He who is without discernment, Let him turn aside to me”; And to those in need of discernment, she says,
9.5: “Com e, eat my bread And drink the wine I mixed for you;
9.6: Forsake lack of discernment, and you shall live; Seek discernment so you may live, And keep straight your understanding with knowledge.” Wisdom: Let Us Attend!
9.7: He who chastises evil men shall receive dishonor to himself, And he who reproves the ungodly man shall be blamed himself.
9.8: Do not reprove evil men, so they may not hate you; Reprovea wise man, and he will love you.
9.9: Give the opportunity to a wise man, and he will be wiser; Instruct a righteous man, and he shall continue to receive it.
9.10: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, And the counsel of saints is understanding; For to know the law is characteristic of a good mind.
9.11: For in this manner you will live a long time, And the years of your life shall be increased.
9.12: My son, if you become wise in yourself, you shall also be wise toward your neighbor; But if you prove to be evil, you alone will go through troubles.
9.13: He who supports him self with lies will shepherd winds And chase flying birds;
9.14: For he abandoned the ways of his own vineyard And strayed from paths of his own farming;
9.15: And he will pass through a waterless desert, A land assigned to drought, And he gathers barrenness with his hands.
9.16: A woman in need of a morsel is without discernment and ov erbold; She has no sense of shame.
9.17: She sits upon the doors of her own house, Upon a seat openly in the streets,
9.18: Calling to those who pass by And who go straight along their paths,
9.19: “He who is very lacking in discernment, let him turn aside to me; And he who is in need of discernment, I exhort, saying,
9.20: ‘Grasp with pleasure the secret bread And the sweet water of theft.’ ”
9.21: But he does not know that the inhabitants of the earth perish beside her, And he happens upon a snare of Hades.
9.22: But hurry off, do not continue in that place, Neither set your eye toward her;
9.23: For so you shall pass through strange water And cross beyond a strange river;
9.24: And keep away from strange water, And do not drink from a strange fountain;
9.25: That you may live a long time And add years of life to yourself.

10.1: A wise son makes his father glad, The Wisdom of Solomon But a son without discernment is a grief to his mother.
10.2: Treasures do not benefit lawless men, But righteousness delivers from death.
10.3: The Lord will not let the soul of the righteous man starve, But He overthrows the life of the ungodly.
10.4: Poverty humbles a man, But the hands of courageous men enrich others.
10.5: A son who is instructed will be wise, And he will use a man without discernment as a servant.
10.6: A son with understanding is kept safe from the heat, But a lawless son is blasted by the wind at harvest time.
10.7: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous man, But untimely grief will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
10.8: The remembrance of the righteous is with eulogies, But the name of an ungodly man is extinguished.
10.9: The wise man in heart will receive the commandments, But the man unguarded in speech will be overthrown in his perverseness.
10.10: He who walks in sincerity walks confidently, But he who perverts his ways will be known.
10.11: He who winks his eyes deceitfully gathers grief for men, But he who reproves boldly is a peacemaker.
10.12: A fountain of life is in the hand of a righteous man, But the mouth of an ungodly man will hide destruction.
10.13: Hatred stirs up strife, But love covers all who are not lovers of strife.
10.14: He who brings forth wisdom from his lips Beats a heartless man with a rod.
10.15: The wise will hide perception, But the mouth of a rash man approaches destruction.
10.16: The acquisition of riches is a fortified city, But poverty is the destruction of the ungodly.
10.17: The works of the righteous produce life, But the fruits of the ungodly produce sins.
10.18: Instruction guards righteous ways of life, But instruction incapable of criticism goes astray.
10.19: Righteous lips cover hatred, But those who bring forth abuse are very lacking in discernment.
10.20: You will not escape sin bya multitude of words, But you of discreet lips will be forbearing.
10.21: The tongue of a righteous man is silver tried in the fire, But the heart of an ungodly man shall fail.
10.22: The lips of righteous men understand lofty things, But men without discernment die in want.
10.23: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous man; It enriches him, and grief of heart will not be added to it.
10.24: A man without discernment does evil things with laughter, But wisdom gives birth to discernment in a man.
10.25: The ungodly man is carried about in destruction, But the desire of the righteous man is acceptable.
10.26: The ungodly man is destroyed by the passing storm, But the righteous man turns aside and shall be saved forever.
10.27: As an unripe grape is harm ful to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, So is a lawless woman to the men who use her.
10.28: The fear of the Lord increases day s, But the years of the ungodly will be shortened.
10.29: Gladness continues for the righteous, But the hope of the ungodly perishes.
10.30: The fear of the Lord is the stronghold of a holy man, But destruction is for those who work evil.
10.31: A righteous man will never fail, But the ungodly shall not inhabit the earth.
10.32: The mouth of a righteous man distills wisdom, But the tongue of an unrighteous man utterly destroys.
10.33: The lips of righteous men distill grace, But the mouth of the ungodly is perverse.

11.1: The Fruits of Righteousness Deceitful scales are an abomination before the Lord, But a righteous weight is acceptable to Him.
11.2: Wherever arrogance enters, there also is dishonor, But the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
11.3: When a righteous man dies, he leaves regret, But the destruction of the ungodly is immediate and brings joy.
11.4: Righteousness cuts straight and blameless paths, But ungodliness embraces wrongdoing.
11.5: The righteousness of upright men delivers them, But lawless men are taken to their destruction.
11.6: When a righteous man dies, his hope does not perish, But the boast of the ungodly perishes.
11.7: A righteous man escapes froma snare, But the ungodly man is handed over in his place.
11.8: There is a snare for citizens in the mouth of the ungodly, But the perception of the righteous is prosperous.
11.9: A city stays upright in the good things of the righteous, But it is razed to the ground by the mouths of the ungodly.
11.10: A man in need of discernment treats citizens with contempt, But a man of discernment keeps quiet.
11.11: A double-tongued man reveals deliberations heard in council, But a man faithful in spirit conceals matters.
11.12: Those for whom there is no leadership fall like leaves, But there is salvation in much counsel.
11.13: A wicked man does evil whenever he meets a righteous man, And he hates the sound of stability.
11.14: A thankful woman raises up glory to her husband, But a throne of dishonor is a woman who hates righteousness.
11.15: Lazy men are in need of wealth, But courageous men support themselves with wealth.
11.16: A merciful man does good to his soul, But an unmerciful man utterly destroys his body.
11.17: An ungodly man does unrighteous works, But the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
11.18: A righteous son is begotten unto life, But the persecution of an ungodly man is unto death.
11.19: Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord, But all who are blameless in their ways are acceptable to Him.
11.20: He who joins hands with the unrighteous will not go unpunished, But he who sows righteousness will receive a faithful reward.
11.21: Like a ring in the nose of a wild swine, So is beauty to an ev il-m inded woman.
11.22: Every desire of the righteous is good, But the hope of the ungodly is destruction.
11.23: There are those who sow their own things and produce more things, And there are those who gather but have less.
11.24: Every sincere soul is blessed, But an angry man is not graceful.
11.25: May the one who hoards grain leave it to the nations, But may blessing be upon the head of the one who shares it.
11.26: He who plans good things seeks good grace, But he who seeks evil, it will capture him.
11.27: He who trusts in riches, this man will fall, But he who helps the righteous, this man will rise.
11.28: He who does not deal graciously with his own house will inherit the wind, And a man without discernment will be servant to one with discernment.
11.29: A tree of life springs up from the fruit of righteousness, But the souls of the lawless will be taken away before their time.
11.30: If the righteous man is scarcely saved, Then where shall an ungodly man and a sinner appear?

12.1: The Riches of Righteousness He who loves instruction loves perception, But he who hates correction is without discernment.
12.2: He who finds grace from the Lord becomes better, But a lawless man will be passed over in silence.
12.3: A man will not prosper by lawlessness, But the roots of righteous men will not be pulled out.
12.4: A courageous wife is a crown to her husband, But as a worm in a tree, so an evildoing wife destroys her husband.
12.5: The thoughts of the righteous are judgments, But the ungodly devise deceits.
12.6: The words of the ungodly are deceitful, But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
12.7: If he does not turn, an ungodly man is destroyed, But the houses of the righteous remain.
12.8: The mouth of a man of understanding is praised bya man, But the slothful of heart are treated with contempt.
12.9: It is better for a man in dishonor to serve himself Than for him to surround him self with honor while in need of bread.
12.10: A righteous man has compassion on the lives of his cattle, But the affections of the ungodly are without mercy.
12.11: He who works his own land will be satisfied with bread, But those who pursue vain things are in need of discernment.
12.12: He who is gladdened by wines in passing his time Shall leave dishonor in his own strongholds.
12.13: The desires of the ungodly are evil, But the roots of the godly are in strongholds.
12.14: By the sin of his lips a sinner falls into snares, But a righteous man escapes from them.
12.15: He whose looks are gentle will show mercy, But he who contends in the gates will afflict souls.
12.16: By the fruits of his mouth, the soul of a man will be filled with good things, And the recompense of his lips will be given to him.
12.17: The ways of undiscerning men are right in their own eyes, But a wise man hearkens to counsels.
12.18: A man without discernment immediately proclaims his wrath, But an astute man hides his own dishonor.
12.19: A righteous man declares his honesty openly, But the witness of the unrighteous is deceitful.
12.20: There are those who wound with a sword as they speak, But the tongues of the wise heal.
12.21: Truthful lips establish a testimony, But a hasty witness has an unrighteous tongue.
12.22: There is deceit in the heart of a man who devises evil things, But those who counsel peace shall be glad.
12.23: Nothing unrighteous will ever be pleasing to the righteous, But the ungodly will be filled with evil things.
12.24: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, But he who shows faithfulness is acceptable to Him.
12.25: A man of understanding is a throne of perception, But the heart of the undiscerning will meet with curses.
12.26: The hand of the chosen shall prevail easily, But the deceitful shall be for captivity.
12.27: A fearful word troubles the heart of a righteous man, But a good message makes him glad.
12.28: A righteous arbiter shall be his own friend, But the decisions of the ungodly are unreasonable.
12.29: Evil things shall pursue sinners, And the way of the ungodly will lead them astray.
12.30: A deceitful man will not gain his prey, But a pure man is a precious possession.
12.31: In the ways of righteousness there is life, But the ways of remembering wrongs are unto death.

13.1: An astute son is obedient to his father, The Godly and the Ungodly But a disobedient son is for destruction.
13.2: A good man eats from the fruits of righteousness, But the souls of the lawless will destroy themselves before their time.
13.3: He who guards his mouth keeps his own soul, But he who is hasty with his lips will dismay himself.
13.4: Every idle man has desire, But the hands of the courageous are diligent.
13.5: A righteous man hates an unrighteous word, But an ungodly man is ashamed and will not have confidence.
13.6: Righteousness guards the simple, But sin makes the ungodly worthless.
13.7: There are those with nothing who make themselves rich, And there are those, though very rich, who humble themselves.
13.8: The ransom of a m an's soul is his own wealth, But the poor man does not withstand a threat.
13.9: Light is with the righteous continually, But the light of the ungodly is extinguished.
13.10: Deceitful souls are led astray in sins, But the righteous have compassion and are merciful.
13.11: An evil man does evil things with arrogance, But those who know themselves are wise.
13.12: Property hastily gained with lawlessness becomes diminished, But he who gathers for him self with godliness will be increased; A righteous man has compassion and lends.
13.13: A man who begins to give aid heartily is better Than he who only promises and leads another to hope; A good desire is a tree of life.
13.14: He who despises a matter will be despised by it, But he who fears the commandment, this man is in good health.
13.15: To a deceitful son there shall be nothing good, But for a wise servant, his deeds shall be prosperous, And his way shall be led aright.
13.16: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, But the man without understanding will die bya snare.
13.17: A good understanding gives grace, And to know the law is to be of a good mind, But the ways of scorners are destructive.
13.18: Every astute man acts with knowledge, But the man without discernment spreads out his own evil.
13.19: A rash king falls into evil things, But a faithful messenger rescues him.
13.20: Instruction removes poverty and dishonor, And he who gives heed to rebukes will be glorified.
13.21: The desires of the godly gladden the soul, But the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
13.22: He who walks with the wise shall be wise, But he who walks with those without discernment will be known.
13.23: Evil things shall pursue sinners, But good things will overtake the righteous.
13.24: A good man will inherit sons of sons, But the wealth of the ungodly will be stored up for the righteous.
13.25: The righteous shall live in wealth many years, But the unrighteous will be destroyed suddenly.
13.26: He who spares the rod hates his son, But he who loves him instructs him with care.
13.27: A righteous man eats and satisfies his soul, But the souls of the ungodly are in want.

14.1: Wise women build houses, Righteousness at Home But those without discernment destroy them with their hands.
14.2: He who walks uprightly fears the Lord, But he who is crooked in his ways will be dishonored.
14.3: From the mouth of a man without discernment comes a rod of arrogance, But the lips of wise men guard themselves.
14.4: Where there are no oxen, the stalls are clean, But where there are abundant crops, the strength of an ox is evident.
14.5: A faithful witness does not lie, But an unrighteous witness kindles lies.
14.6: You will seek wisdom in the company of evil men, and you will not find it; But perception is easily found with the discerning.
14.7: All things are contrary to a man without discernment, But the weapons of perception are wise lips.
14.8: The wisdom of astute men will know their ways, But the folly of men without discernment is in their deceit.
14.9: The houses of the lawless are due for purification, But the houses of the righteous are acceptable.
14.10: If the heart of a man is controlled by feelings, his soul is sorrowful, But when he rejoices, it is not mingled with arrogance.
14.11: The houses of the ungodly will be destroy ed, But the tents of the upright shall stand.
14.12: There is a road that seems to be right with men, But the ends of it reach into the depths of Hades.
14.13: Sorrow does not mingle with gladness, But in the end, this joy turns to sorrow.
14.14: A bold-hearted man will be filled with his own ways, But a good man with all his thoughts.
14.15: A simple man believes in every word, But an astute man comes to repentance.
14.16: A wise man fears and turns away from evil, But a man without discernment persuades himself to mingle with a lawless man.
14.17: A quick-tem pered man acts with recklessness, But a man with discernment bears many things.
14.18: Men without discernment will share in evil, But the astute will take hold of perception.
14.19: Evil men will slip and fall in the presence of good men, And the ungodly shall serve at the gate of the righteous.
14.20: Friends will hate poor friends, But the friends of the rich are many.
14.21: He who dishonors the poor sins, But he who has mercy on the poor is very blessed.
14.22: Deceivers devise evil things, But good men devise mercy and truth.
14.23: Devisers of evil things do not understand mercy and faithfulness, But mercies and faithfulness are with devisers of good things.
14.24: To everyone who is careful there is an abundance, But he who is pleasure-taking and slothful shall be in want.
14.25: The crown of the wise is astuteness, But the pastime of the undiscerning is evil.
14.26: A faithful witness will rescue a soul from evil men, But a deceitful man kindles lies.
14.27: In the fear of the Lord there is hope of strength, And to His children there remains support.
14.28: The command of the Lord is a fountain of life, For it causes one to turn from the snare of death.
14.29: The glory of a king is in a large nation, But the destruction of a ruler is in a lack of people.
14.30: A longsuffering man is strong in discernment, But the fainthearted man is strongly without discernment.
14.31: A man with a gentle spirit is a healer of the heart, But a sensual heart is the moth of the bones.
14.32: He who oppresses the poor provokes his Maker, But he who honors Him has mercy upon a poor man.
14.33: In his evil an ungodly man will be rejected, But a righteous man has confidence in his own holiness.
14.34: There is wisdom in the good heart of a man, But wisdom is unknown in the heart of those without discernment.
14.35: Righteousness exalts a nation, But sins dim inish tribes.
14.36: A wise servant is acceptable to a king, And by his own versatilityhe removes dishonor.

15.1: Righteous Responses Wrath destroy seven men of discernment; But a humble answer turns away anger, And a grievous word stirs up wrath.
15.2: The tongue of the wise understands good things, But the mouth of those without discernment proclaims evil things.
15.3: The eyes of the Lord are in every place; They keep watch over both the evil and the good.
15.4: The healing of the tongue is a tree of life, And the one who guards it will be filled with the Spirit.
15.5: A son without discernment treats the instruction of his father with contempt, But the one who guards his commandments is more astute.
15.6: In abundant righteousness there is much strength, But the ungodly shall utterly perish from the earth.
15.7: In the houses of the righteous there is much strength, But the fruits of the ungodly shall perish.
15.8: The lips of the wise are bound by perception, But the hearts of those without discernment are not safe.
15.9: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, But the prayers of the upright are acceptable with Him.
15.10: The ways of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, But He loves those who pursue righteousness.
15.11: The instruction of the simple is known by those who pass by, But those who hate reproofs will die shamefully.
15.12: Hades and destruction are manifest before the Lord; How can the hearts of men not be also?
15.13: An uninstructed man will not love those who reprove him, And he will not keep company with the wise.
15.14: When one's heart is glad, his face is cheerful, But when it is in grief, his face is sad.
15.15: The upright heart seeks perception, But the mouth of the uninstructed will know evil things.
15.16: The eyes of evil men are waiting for evil things all the time, But good men are at rest continually.
15.17: Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord Than great treasures with lack of fear.
15.18: Better is a dinner of herbs with friendship and grace Than a fatted calf with hostility.
15.19: An angry man stirs up contention, But a longsuffering man even calms the rising quarrel.
15.20: A longsuffering man will extinguish condem nations, But the ungodly man stirs up more.
15.21: The ways of idle men are strewn with thorny plants, But the thorny plants of the courageous are worn smooth.
15.22: A wise son gladdens a father, But a son without discernment treats his mother with contempt.
15.23: The paths of one without understanding are in need of discernment, But a man with discernment walks uprightly.
15.24: Those not honoring councils defer their deliberations, But counsel remains in the hearts of those who resolve to do it.
15.25: The evil man will not obey counsel, Nor will he speak anything appropriate, even something for the common good.
15.26: The thoughts of a wise man are his ways of life, That he might turn aside and be saved from Hades.
15.27: The Lord will destroy the houses of the arrogant, But He will strengthen the boundary of a widow.
15.28: The thinking of the unrighteous man is an abomination to the Lord, But the words of the holy are sacred.
15.29: He who receives bribes utterly destroys himself, But he who hates the receiving of bribes saves himself.
15.30: Sins are cleansed by almsgiving and faithfulness, And by the fear of the Lord everyone turns aside from evil.
15.31: The hearts of the righteous care about faithfulness, But the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things.
15.32: The ways of righteous men are acceptable before the Lord, And through them even enemies become friends.
15.33: God is far from the ungodly, But He hears the pray ers of the righteous.
15.34: Better is a small yield with the righteous Than abundant fruits with the unrighteous.
15.35: Let the heart of a man think righteous things That he may make his steps straight under God.
15.36: The eye that beholds good things gladdens the heart, But a good report enriches the bones.
15.37: He who rejects instruction hates him self, But he who gives heed to reproofs loves his soul.
15.38: The fear of God is instruction and wisdom, And the beginning of glory will respond to it.

16.1: Humility, Discernment, and Righteousness All the works of the humble are evident before the Lord, But the ungodly will be destroyed in the evil day.
16.2: Every high-hearted man is unclean before the Lord, And he who joins hands with the unrighteous will not go unpunished.
16.3: The beginning of a good way is to do righteous things, And this is more acceptable to God than to offer sacrifices.
16.4: He who seeks the Lord will find knowledge with righteousness, And those who seek Him rightly will find peace.
16.5: All the works of the Lord are with righteousness, But the ungodly man is kept for an evil day.
16.6: There is an oracle on the lips of a king, And his mouth does not err in judgment.
16.7: The weight of a scale is righteousness before the Lord, For His works are righteous standards.
16.8: He who does evil things is an abomination to a king, For the throne of a ruler is prepared with righteousness.
16.9: Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, And he loves upright words.
16.10: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, But a wise man will appease him.
16.11: The son of a king is in the light of life, And those acceptable to him are as a cloud of the latter rain.
16.12: The abodes of wisdom are more to be chosen than gold, And the abodes of discernment are more to be chosen than silver.
16.13: The paths of life turn away from evil, And the ways of righteousness are length of life;
16.14: He who receives instruction shall be in good things, And he who heeds rebukes shall become wise;
16.15: He who guards his own ways shall keep his own soul, And he who loves his life shall use his mouth sparingly.
16.16: Arrogance goes before destruction And folly before a fall.
16.17: A gentle mind with humility is better Than he who divides spoils with the arrogant.
16.18: A man wise in his deeds is a discoverer of good things, But he who trusts in God is the most blessed.
16.19: Men call the wise and understanding worthless, But those pleasing in speech will increase in understanding.
16.20: Understanding is a fountain of life to those who possess it, But the instruction of those without discernment is evil.
16.21: The heart of a wise man shall understand the things from his own mouth, And he shall carry knowledge upon his lips.
16.22: Good words are a honeycomb, And their sweetness is a healing of the soul.
16.23: There are ways that seem right to a man; However, their ends look to the depths of Hades.
16.24: A man labors diligently for himself And expels destruction from him self; However, a perverse man carries destruction on his lips.
16.25: A man without discernment digs up evil things for himself And stores up fire on his own lips.
16.26: A perverse man spreads evil things, And a torch of deceit kindles evils and separates friends.
16.27: A lawless man makes a trial of friends And leads them in ways not good.
16.28: A man sets his eyes to calculate perverse things And determines every evil thing with his lips; This man is a furnace of wickedness.
16.29: Old age is a crown of dignity, But it is found in the ways of righteousness.
16.30: A patient man is better than a strong man, And he who controls his temper is better than he who captures a city.
16.31: All evil things come into the bosom s of the unrighteous, But all righteous things come from the Lord.

17.1: Family and Friends Better is a morsel with enjoyment in peace Than a house full of many good things and unrighteous sacrifices with quarreling.
17.2: A servant with discernment shall rule over masters without discernment, And will divide portions among brethren.
17.3: As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, So are chosen hearts before the Lord.
17.4: An evil man heeds the tongue of the lawless, But a righteous man pays no attention to false lips.
17.5: He who laughs at the poor provokes the One who made him, And he who rejoices in destruction will not be unpunished; But he who has compassion will be shown mercy.
17.6: The crown of old men is children of children, And the boasting of children is their fathers.
17.7: The entire world of goods belongs to the faithful, But to the faithless, not even a penny.
17.8: Faithful lips will not adapt to a man without discernment, Nor lying lips to a righteous man.
17.9: Instruction awards benefits to those using it, And wherever it turns, it prospers them.
17.10: He who hides wrongdoings seeks love, But he who hates to cover them will separate friends and close relatives.
17.11: A threat breaks the heart of a man with discernment, But a man without discernment, though flogged, has no perception.
17.12: Every evil man stirs up controversy, But the Lord will send him a m erciless messenger.
17.13: Care will befall a thoughtful man, But men without discernment devise evil things.
17.14: He who repays evil for good, Evil will not be removed from his house.
17.15: The foundation of righteousness gives authority to words, But discord and quarreling precede poverty.
17.16: He who judges the unrighteous as righteous, and the righteous as unrighteous, He is unclean and abominable before God.
17.17: Why do goods belong to a man without discernment? For a heartless man is unable to gain wisdom.
17.18: He who makes his own house lofty seeks destruction, And the one who turns away from learning will fall into evils.
17.19: Let a friend be with you on every occasion, And let brethren be useful in necessities, For they are begotten for this reason.
17.20: A man without discernment applauds and rejoices over himself, As also the one who gives himself as surety for his friend.
17.21: He who loves sin rejoices in quarrels, And the hard-hearted man does not assemble with good men.
17.22: A changeable man will fall into evils with his tongue, And a heart without discernment is grief to the one possessing it.
17.23: A father does not delight in an uninstructed son; But a son with discernment gladdens his mother.
17.24: A cheerful heart makes a man healthy, But the bones of a sorrowful man dry him up.
17.25: The ways of a man who receives gifts unrighteous ly do not prosper, And the ungodly man shuns the ways of righteousness.
17.26: The face of a wise man shows understanding, But the eyes of the man without discernment are upon the ends of the earth.
17.27: A son without discernment is wrath to a father And grief to her who bore him.
17.28: It is not good to punish a righteous man, Nor is it holy to plot against righteous princes.
17.29: He who refrains from uttering a harsh word is intelligent, And a longsuffering man has discernment.
17.30: Wisdom shall be imputed to a man without understanding who asks for wisdom, And anyone who holds his peace will seem to have discernment.

18.1: Words and Works A man seeks a pretext when he wishes to separate from his friends, But he shall be reproached at every opportunity.
18.2: A man lacking understanding has no need of wisdom, For he is rather led by lack of discernment.
18.3: When an ungodly man comes into the depth of evil things, he acts contemptuously, But dishonor and reproach come upon him.
18.4: A word in the heart of a man is deep water, And a river and a fountain of life spring up from it.
18.5: It is not good to admire the person of the ungodly, Nor is it holy to pervert righteousness in judgment.
18.6: The lips of a man without discernment lead him into evil things, And his rash mouth calls upon death.
18.7: The mouth of a man without discernment is destruction to him, And his lips are the snare of his soul.
18.8: Fear destroys slothful men, And the souls of cowardly men shall hunger.
18.9: He who does not heal him self by his works, He is the brother of him who maltreats himself.
18.10: The name of the Lord is of great strength, And when the righteous run to it, they are exalted.
18.11: The substance of a rich man is a strong city, And its glory casts a great shadow.
18.12: Before its destruction, the heart of a man exalts itself, And before its glory, it humbles itself.
18.13: He who replies to a word before he hears it Lacks discernment, and this is a reproach to him.
18.14: A servant with discernment calms the anger of a man, But who can support a discouraged man?
18.15: A heart of discernment gains perception, And the ears of the wise seek understanding.
18.16: The gift of a man enlarges him And seats him beside princes.
18.17: When a prosecutor speaks first, he seems righteous, But when the defendant examines his case, he is reproved.
18.18: An allotment of land ends controversies, And it determines the boundary between princes.
18.19: A brother aided by his brother is like a strong and fortified city, And he is strong like a well-founded palace.
18.20: From the fruits of his mouth a man fills his stomach, And from the fruits of his lips he will fill him self to the full.
18.21: Life and death are in the hand of a tongue, And those who rule over it will eat the fruits thereof.
18.22: He who finds a good wife finds benefits And receives cheerfulness from God.
18.23: He who casts out a good wife casts out good things, And he who keeps adulteresses is without discernment and is ungodly.

19.1: Mercy and Malice A m an's lack of discernment maltreats his ways, And in his heart he blames God.
19.2: Wealth adds many friends, But the poor man is even forsaken by an existing friend.
19.3: A false witness shall not be unpunished, And he who accuses unrighteous ly shall not escape.
19.4: Many men serve in the presence of kings, But every evil man becomes a reproach to another man.
19.5: Every man who hates his poor brother, He shall be far from friendship.
19.6: Good understanding will draw near those who know it, And a man with discernment will find it.
19.7: He who does many evil things perfects wickedness, And he who provokes with words, He shall not be saved.
19.8: He who gains discernment loves himself, And he who guards discernment will find good things.
19.9: A false witness shall not be unpunished, And he who kindles evil will perish by it.
19.10: Luxury is not profitable for a man without discernment, And it is not good if a servant begins to rule with arrogance.
19.11: A merciful man is longsuffering, And his boast goes against the lawless.
19.12: The anger of a king is like the roar of a lion, But as dew upon the grass, thus is his grace.
19.13: A son without discernment is a disgrace to his father, And vows paid from the wage of a prostitute are not pure.
19.14: Fathers divide the house and property to their children, But a wife is suited to her husband by God.
19.15: Cowardice possesses a weak man, And the soul of the idle man will be hungry.
19.16: He who guards the commandment keeps his soul, But he who despises his ways shall perish.
19.17: The one who has mercy on the poor lends to God, And He will repay him according to his gift.
19.18: Instruct your son, for thus he shall be hopeful, But do not lift up your soul in arrogance.
19.19: A malicious man shall be punished severely, And if he commits injury, he will also add this to his soul.
19.20: Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, That you may become wise in your last days.
19.21: There are many thoughts in the heart of a man, But the counsel of the Lord abides forever.
19.22: Mercy is fruit to a man, And a poor righteous man is better than a rich liar.
19.23: The fear of the Lord is unto life for a man, And he shall lodge without fear in places where knowledge is not examined.
19.24: A man who hides his hands in his bosom unrighteous ly, He will not even bring them up to his mouth.
19.25: When a pestilent man is punished, a man without discernment becomes more astute, But if you reprovea discerning man, he will understand perception.
19.26: He who dishonors his father and pushes away his mother, He will be shamed and reproached.
19.27: A son who forsakes guarding his father's instruction, He will think about evil sayings.
19.28: He who becomes surety for an undiscerning child despises the ordinance, And the mouth of the ungodly swallows judgments.
19.29: Lashes are prepared for the intem perate And punishments for the shoulders of those without discernment.

20.1: Double Standards or Single-Mindedness Wine is an intem perate thing, and strong drink is full of violence; And all who commingle with it will not be wise.
20.2: The threat of a king does not differ from the anger of a lion, And he who provokes him sins against his own soul.
20.3: It is glory for a man to turn away from reproaches, But every man without discernment is entangled with such things.
20.4: A lazy man who is reproached feels no shame; Likewise also is he who borrows bread in harvest.
20.5: Counsel is deep water in the heart of a man, And a man with discernment will draw it out.
20.6: Man is important, and a man who shows mercy is noble, But it is difficult to find a faithful man.
20.7: He who lives blameless ly in righteousness, He will leave blessed children behind him.
20.8: When a righteous king sits upon the throne, No evil thing can oppose his presence.
20.9: Who will boast about having a pure heart? Or who will declare boldly being clean from sins?
20.10: The lamp of him who reviles his father or mother shall be put out, And the pupils of his eyes shall see darkness.
20.11: A portion gained hastily in the beginning Will not be blessed at the end.
20.12: Do not say, “I will avenge myself on the enemy,” But wait on the Lord, that you may be helped.
20.13: A weight, great and small, and a double standard, Both are also unclean before the Lord.
20.14: And the one who uses these things in his pursuits will be entangled; But a young man with holiness, his road is straight.
20.15: The ear hears and the eye sees; Both are also works of the Lord.
20.16: Do not love to speak ill, That you may not be taken away;
20.17: Open your eyes, And you will be filled with bread.
20.18: A double standard is an abomination to the Lord, And a deceitful scale is not good before Him.
20.19: Steps are made straight for a man by the Lord, But how can a mortal man understand His ways?
20.20: It is a snare for a man to quickly sanctify something of his own things as holy, Then after making this vow, to come to a change of heart.
20.21: A wise king is a winnower of the ungodly, And he casts them upon the wheel of torture.
20.22: The breath of man is the light of the Lord, Who searches the inner man.
20.23: Mercy and truth are a guard for the king, And they will encircle his throne with righteousness.
20.24: Wisdom is an ornament to young men, And the glory of old men is their gray hair.
20.25: Bruises and fractures happen to evil men, And plagues shall come into their inner man.

21.1: Godliness: Willing to Do God's Will As a flow of water, so is the heart of the king in the hand of God; Wherever He wills to incline it, there he turns it.
21.2: Every man appears righteous to himself, But the Lord makes hearts right.
21.3: To do righteous things and to speak the truth Are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.
21.4: A high-m inded man is bold-hearted in his arrogance, And the lamp of the ungodly is sin.
21.5: He who produces treasures with a lying tongue Pursues worthless things upon the snares of death.
21.6: Destruction shall entertain the ungodly, For they are not willing to do righteous things.
21.7: To the crooked, God sends crooked way s, For His works are pure and upright.
21.8: It is better to dwell in a corner in the open air Than with wrongdoing in plastered rooms and in a shared house.
21.9: The soul of the ungodly will not be shown mercy by anyone among men.
21.10: When the intem perate man is punished, the simple man becomes more astute, And a wise man of understanding shall receive knowledge.
21.11: A righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly, And he despises the ungodly in their evils.
21.12: He who closes his ears that he might not listen to the weak, He will also call upon someone, and there will be no one listening.
21.13: A secret gift calms anger, But he who refrains from giving gifts stirs up strong anger.
21.14: It is the joy of the righteous to do judgment, But a holy man is unclean before evildoers.
21.15: A man who wanders from the way of righteousness Shall rest in an assembly of giants.
21.16: A man in need loves merriment, Loving wine and oil as wealth.
21.17: A lawless man is the outcast of a righteous man.
21.18: It is better to live in a desert Than with a contentious, talkative, and quick-tem pered woman.
21.19: A treasury of desire will rest upon the mouth of a wise man, But men without discernment shall swallow it.
21.20: The way of righteousness and mercy shall find life and glory.
21.21: A wise man assaults fortified cities And pulls down the stronghold the ungodly trust.
21.22: He who guards his mouth and tongue Keeps his soul from tribulation.
21.23: A troublemaker is called rash, arrogant, and boastful, And he who bears malice is called lawless.
21.24: Desires kill a slothful man, For his hands choose not to do any thing.
21.25: The ungodly man desires evil all day long, But the righteous man shows mercy and compassion unsparingly.
21.26: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, For they offer them lawlessly.
21.27: A false witness shall perish, But an obedient man will speak guardedly.
21.28: An ungodly man resists shame less ly to the face, But the upright man himself understands his ways.
21.29: There is no wisdom, there is no courage, There is no counsel for the ungodly.
21.30: The horse is prepared for the day of war, But help is from the Lord.

22.1: Rich Man, Poor Man A good name is to be chosen more than much wealth, And good grace more than silver and gold.
22.2: The rich man and the poor man meet with one another, But the Lord made both.
22.3: An astute man, seeing an evil man severely punished, is himself instructed, But those passing by without discernment suffer loss.
22.4: The fear of the Lord and riches and glory and life Are the offspring of wisdom.
22.5: Thorns and snares are in the ways of the crooked, But he who guards his own soul will keep away from them.
22.6: The rich will rule over the poor, And servants will lend to their own masters.
22.7: He who sows worthless things will reap evil things, And bring to an end the plague of his works.
22.8: God blesses a cheerful man and a giver, And he will bring to an end the vanity of his works.
22.9: He who shows mercy to a poor man shall himself be supported, For he gave his own bread to the poor man.
22.10: He who gives gifts to a poor man gains victory and honor for himself; However, he who buys him takes away his soul.
22.11: Cast out a pestilent man from the assembly, And contention will go out with him; For whenever he sits in the assembly, he dishonors everyone.
22.12: The Lord loves holy hearts, And all the blameless are acceptable to Him;
22.14: And the eyes of the Lord maintain perception, But the lawless man despises His words.
22.15: A slothful man makes excuses and says, “There is a lion in the way, and murderers in the streets.”
22.16: The mouth of a lawless man is a deep pit, And the man hated by the Lord shall fall into it.
22.17: Evil ways are before a man, And he does not love to turn away from them, But it is necessary to turn away froma crooked and evil way.
22.18: Folly fastens itself to the heart of a child, For the rod and instruction are far from him.
22.19: He who oppresses a poor man increases his possessions, Yet he gives them to a rich man to lessen them.
22.20: Incline your ear to the words of the wise and hear my word, And establish your heart, that you may know they are good.
22.21: And if you apply them to your heart, They will gladden you and at the same time be upon your lips;
22.22: That your hope might be in the Lord, And His way might be known to you.
22.23: And register them upon the breadth of your heart for yourself threefold, For counsel and knowledge.
22.24: Therefore, I teach you a true word and good knowledge to be obeyed, That you might answer words of truth to those who question you.
22.25: Do not rob the poor, for he is needy, And do not dishonor the helpless at the gates;
22.26: For the Lord will judge his cause, And you will deliver your soul from violence.
22.27: Do not be a companion to an angry man And do not associate with a quick-tem pered friend,
22.28: Lest you learn his ways And receive a snare for your soul.
22.29: Do not give yourself as surety because you respect a person, For if you do not have the wherewithal to make compensation, They will take your bed out from under you.
22.30: Do not remove the eternal landmarks your fathers established.
22.31: An observant man and one astute in his business Should be present with kings, And he should not be present with slothful men.

23.1: Understanding and Priorities If you sit down to dine at a table of princes, Understand carefully the things put before you;
23.2: And apply your hand, Knowing you should prepare certain things;
23.3: And if you are insatiable, do not desire its delicacies, For these things belong to a false life.
23.4: If you are poor, do not measure yourself with a rich man, But keep away from this in your thinking;
23.5: If you fix your eye on him, he will disappear, For wings like an eagle's are prepared for him, And he returns to the house of his master.
23.6: Do not dine with an envious man, Neither desire his foods;
23.7: For as someone who may swallow a hair, So he eats and drinks.
23.8: Neither invite him in, nor eat your morsel with him; For he will vomit it forth and m altreat your good words.
23.9: Speak nothing into the ears of a man without discernment, Lest he treat your wise words with contempt.
23.10: Do not remove the eternal landmarks, And do not enter the possession of orphans.
23.11: For the Lord who redeems them is mighty, And He will judge their cause with you.
23.12: Give your heart to instruction, And prepare your ears for words of perception.
23.13: Do not withhold instruction from a child, For if you should strike him with a rod, he would not die;
23.14: For you shall strike him with a rod And deliver his soul from death.
23.15: My son, if your heart becomes wise, You will also gladden my heart;
23.16: And your lips shall spend time with the words on my lips, If they be upright.
23.17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, But be in fear of the Lord the whole day long.
23.18: For if you keep these words, you shall have offspring, And your hope will not depart from you. A Father's Counsel on Wine and Women
23.19: Hear, my son, and become wise, And direct aright the thoughts of your heart.
23.20: Do not be a wine-bibber, Neither provide contributions of meats or goods at drinking parties.
23.21: For every drunkard and fornicator shall become impoverished, And every sluggard shall clothe himself with tattered and ragged garments.
23.22: Hear, my son, your father who begot you, And do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
23.23: A righteous father rears his child well, And his soul rejoices in a wise son.
23.24: Let your father and mother be glad in you, And let her who bore you rejoice.
23.25: My son, give me your heart, And let your eyes observe my ways;
23.26: For a house of prostitution is a pierced vessel And a strange and empty well;
23.27: For he shall perish suddenly, And every lawless man shall be destroyed.
23.28: Who has woe? Who has tumult? Who has condemnation? Who has unpleasantness and gossip? Who has afflictions with no purpose? Whose eyes are pale?
23.29: Is it not those who linger long with wines? Is it not those who hunt for the whereabouts of drinking parties?
23.30: Do not be drunk with wine, but keep company with righteous men, And keep company in public walks;
23.31: For if you set your eyes to the bowls and cups, Afterward you will walk about more naked than ground meat.
23.32: And at last, he stretches him self out as one bitten by a serpent, And the venom spreads through him as one bitten bya horned serpent.
23.33: When your eyes behold a strange woman, Then your mouth will speak twisted things;
23.34: And you will lie down as in the heart of the sea And as a pilot in a great storm;
23.35: And you will say, “They beat me, but I did not suffer, And they mocked me, but I knew it not;
23.36: When will it be morning, That I may go seek those with whom I may company?”

24.1: My son, do not envy evil men, Issues of Life and Death Neither desire to be with them;
24.2: For their heart ponders a lie, And their lips speak of sufferings.
24.3: A house is built with wisdom, And it is built up with understanding.
24.4: Storehouses are filled with perception From all honorable and good riches.
24.5: It is better to be a wise man of strength And a man having discernment, than to be a man who has a large estate.
24.6: War comes with the skill of a commander, But help comes with the heart of a counselor.
24.7: Wisdom and good thinking are in the gates of the wise; The wise do not turn away from the mouth of the Lord, But they deliberate with councils;
24.8: Death happens to the uninstructed, And a man without discernment shall die in his sins;
24.9: And uncleanness will pollute a pestilent man In an evil day and a day of tribulation, until he dies.
24.10: Rescue those being led into death, And saw off the bonds of those being cast out; do not spare them help;
24.11: If you say, “I do not know this man,” Know that the Lord knows the hearts of all;
24.12: And He who formed every breath knows all things, Who will render to each man according to his works.
24.13: My son, eat honey, for the honeycomb is good, That your throat may be sweetened.
24.14: Thus you shall discern wisdom for your soul, For if you find it, there will be a good end to your life; And hope will not abandon you.
24.15: Do not bring an ungodly man to the dwelling of the righteous, Neither be deceived by the full satisfaction of the stomach.
24.16: For a righteous man will fall seven times and rise again, But the ungodly shall weaken in evils.
24.17: If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, And do not exalt yourself at his stumbling;
24.18: Because the Lord will see this, and it will not please Him, And He will turn His anger from him.
24.19: Do not rejoice in evildoers, Nor envy sinners;
24.20: For there is no future for evil men, And the lamp of the ungodly shall be put out.
24.21: Fear God, my son, and the king, And disobey neither of them;
24.22: For suddenly they will take retribution on the ungodly, And who will know the punishments of both?
24.23: A son who guards the word will be free from destruction, For he receives it fully.
24.24: Let no lie be spoken from your tongue to the king, And let no lie come from his tongue.
24.25: The tongue of the king is a sword and not of flesh, And whoever it delivers, it will annihilate;
24.26: For if his anger is sharpened, It destroys men with its sinews.
24.27: And it dev ours the bones of men, And it burns like a flame, So as to be inedible for the nestlings of eagles.
24.28: Now I say the following to you, the wise, to observe, “It is not good to be partial in judgment.”
24.29: He who says about an ungodly man, “He is righteous,” Shall be accursed to people and despicable to nations;
24.30: But those who reprove him shall appear more excellent, And a good blessing shall come upon them; And they will kiss the lips that answer good words.
24.31: Prepare your works for your going forth, And prepare yourself for the field;
24.32: And walk behind me, And you shall build up your house.
24.33: Do not be a false witness against your country man, Neither open wide your lips;
24.34: Do not say, “I will treat him as he treated me, And I shall avenge myself on him wherein he wronged me.”
24.35: A man without discernment is like a field, And a man in need of discernment is like a vineyard;
24.36: If you leave it alone, it will remain dry and barren, Altogether covered with grass and forsaken, And its stone walls will be razed to the ground.
24.37: Afterward, I repented; I observed that I might choose instruction.
24.38: I doze a little, and I sleep a little, And I fold my arms across my chest a little.
24.39: If you do this, your poverty shall go before you, And want, like a strong runner.

25.1: These are the miscellaneous instructions of Solomon which the friends of Hezekiah, the King of Judah, wrote out.
25.2: The Glory of God hides a word, And the glory of the king honors deeds.
25.3: Heaven is high, and earth is deep, But the heart of the king is incapable of disproof.
25.4: Beat drossy silver, And it will be made entirely clean.
25.5: Slay the ungodly from before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.
25.6: Do not brag on yourself in the presence of the king, Neither stand in the places of princes;
25.7: For it is better that it be said to you, “Com eup to me,” Than for you to be humbled in the presence of a prince.
25.8: Speak the things your eyes see.
25.9: Do not enter into a quarrel quickly, That you may not be sorry in the end.
25.10: When your friend reproaches you, Retreat and do not despise him,
25.11: Lest your friend continue to reproach you, And your quarrel and enmity shall not depart, But be equal to death for you.
25.12: Grace and friendship free a man; Keep these for yourself, that you may not be reproached, But guard your ways peaceably.
25.13: As a golden apple in a small necklace of sardius stone, Thus it is to speak a wise word.
25.14: As a veryexpensivesardius stone set in a golden earring, So is a wise word to an obedient ear.
25.15: As the falling of snow in harvest is beneficial against the heat, So is a faithful messenger to those who send him; For he benefits the souls of those who use him.
25.16: As winds, clouds, and rains are evident, So are those who boast in a false gift.
25.17: There is prosperity for kings in patience, And a mild tongue breaks bones.
25.18: When you find honey, eat what is sufficient, Lest being filled, you should vomit it up.
25.19: Seldom visit your own friend's house, Lest he become fed up with your company and hate you.
25.20: As a club, a sword, and a pointed arrow, So also is the man who testifies as a false witness against his friend.
25.21: The tooth of an evil man and the foot of a lawless man Shall perish in an evil day.
25.22: As vinegar is bad for a festering wound, So calamity befalling the body grieves the heart.
25.23: As a moth in a garment and a worm in wood, So the grief of a man dam ages the heart.
25.24: If your enemy is hungry, feed him, And if he is thirsty, give him drink.
25.25: For by doing this, you shall heap coals of fire on his head, And the Lord will reward you with good things.
25.26: The north wind stirs up clouds, And a sham eless face provokes the tongue.
25.27: It is better to dwell in a corner on a housetop Than in a house shared with an abusive woman.
25.28: As cold water is agreeable to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far-off land.
25.29: As if someone would stop a spring and corrupt an outlet of water, So it is unseemly for a righteous man to fall before the ungodly.
25.30: It is not good to eat too much honey, But it is necessary to honor words held in honor.
25.31: As an unfortified city whose walls are broken down, So is a man who does something without counsel.

26.1: The Undiscerning Man As dew in harvest and as rain in summer, So honor is not for a man without discernment.
26.2: As birds and sparrows fly, So a curse will not come upon anyone without a cause.
26.3: As a whip for a horse and a prod for a donkey, So is a rod for a lawless nation.
26.4: Do not answer an undiscerning man in relation to his lack of discernment, Lest you become like him.
26.5: But answer an undiscerning man contrary to his lack of discernment, So he may not appear wise to himself.
26.6: He shall drink reproach at his own feet Who sends a word through an undiscerning messenger.
26.7: Remove the motion of the legs And a proverb from the mouth of men without discernment.
26.8: He who binds a stone in a sling Is like one who gives glory to a man without discernment.
26.9: Thorny plants grow in the hand of a drunkard And slavery in the hand of men without discernment.
26.10: All flesh of men without discernment grievously suffers many things, For their illusion is brought to nothing.
26.11: As when a dog returns to his own vomit and becomes despicable, So is a man without discernment who returns to his own evil by his own sin.
26.12: There is shame that brings on sin, And there is shame that is glory and grace.
26.13: I sawa man who seemed to himself to be wise, But a man without discernment has more hope than he. The Slothful Man
26.14: A slothful man who is sent on his way says, “There is a lion in the way.”
26.15: As a door turns upon its hinge, So does a slothful man upon his bed.
26.16: When a slothful man hides his hand in his bosom, He shall be unable to bring it to his mouth.
26.17: A slothful man appears wiser to himself Than he who satisfactorilybrings back a message. The Scheming Man
26.18: As he who layshold of a dog's tail, So is he who is the mouthpiece of another's cause.
