26.19: As those who need correction speak to others, He who first replies to the word shall be tripped up,
26.20: So are all who set a trap for their own friends; But when they are discovered, they say, “I did it in jest.”
26.21: A fire rages among many trees, But where there is no disagreement, contention is at rest.
26.22: As a fireplace is for coals and wood for a fire, So a contentious man kindles violence.
26.23: The words of a talebearer are mild And they strike into the innermost affections.
26.24: Money given with deceit is like a sharp piece of broken pottery; So smooth lips hide a heart that causes pain.
26.25: A weeping enemy promises everything with his lips, But in his heart he devises deceits.
26.26: If your enemy entreats you with a loud voice, Do not consent, for there are seven vices in his soul.
26.27: He who hides enmity co nt riv es deceit, But being well known in the assemblies, he exposes his own sins.
26.28: He who digs a pit for his neighbor shall fall into it, And he who rolls a stone rolls it upon him self.
26.29: A lying tongue hates the truth, And an unguarded mouth causes confusion.

27.1: Do not boast about tomorrow, Wisdom for Today For you do not know what the next day will bring forth.
27.2: Let your neighbor praise you, and not your own mouth; A stranger, and not your own lips.
27.3: A stone is heavy, and sand is cumbersome; But the wrath of a man without discernment is heavier than both.
27.4: Wrath is m erciless and anger passionate, But jealousy supports nothing.
27.5: Open reproofs are better than hidden love.
27.6: The wounds of a friend are more trustworthy Than the voluntary kisses of an enemy.
27.7: A satiated soul mocks honey combs, But to a hungry soul, even bitter things appear sweet.
27.8: As when a bird flies down from its own nest, So is a man enslaved whenever he becomes a fugitivefromhis own place.
27.9: The heart delights in perfumes, wines, and incenses, But the soul is broken by mishaps.
27.10: Do not abandon your friend or the friend of your father, And when you have misfortune, do not go to your brother's house; A friend nearby is better than a brother far away.
27.11: My son, become wise, that my heart may be glad, And turn away from your reproachful words.
27.12: An astute man hides when evils are at hand, But when men without discernment are at hand, they will pay the penalty.
27.13: If a haughty man passes by, take away his garment, For he lays waste the goods of another.
27.14: Whoever blesses a friend early in the morning with a loud voice, He will not seem different from one who curses him.
27.15: Continual dripping on a rainydaydrives a man from his house; In like manner, a contentious woman also drives a man from his own house.
27.16: The north wind is a harsh wind, And a prosperous man is called harsh.
27.17: Iron sharpens iron, And a man sharpens the countenance of his friend.
27.18: Whoever plants a fig tree will eat its fruit, And whoever guards his own master will be honored.
27.19: As faces are not like other faces, So neither are the hearts of men.
27.20: Hades and destruction are not satiated; In like manner the eyes of men are also insatiable.
27.21: He whose eye is fixed is an abomination to the Lord, And the uninstructed are intem perate with the tongue.
27.22: Proving by fire is a way of testing for silver and gold, But a man is tested by the mouth of those who praise him.
27.23: A lawless heart seeks evil things, But an upright heart seeks knowledge.
27.24: If you should whip a man without discernment in the midst of the council and dishonor him, You would not remove his lack of discernment.
27.25: Know thoroughly the souls of your sheep, And you will set your heart on your flocks,
27.26: Since strength and might are not in man forever, Neither are they transmitted from generation to generation.
27.27: Take care of the green plants in the field, and cut the herbs short, And gather the grass of the mountains.
27.28: That you may have the wool of sheep for clothing, Honor the field, so there may be lambs for you.
27.29: My son, you have strong sayings from me for your life And for the life of your servants.

28.1: The Lawful and the Lawless An ungodly man flees when no one is pursuing, But a righteous man is confident as a lion.
28.2: Condem nations arise because of the sins of the ungodly, But an astute man quenches them.
28.3: A bold man harasses the poor with ungodliness. As a driving and unprofitable rain,
28.4: So those who forsake the law praise ungodliness, But those who love the law surround themselves with a wall.
28.5: Evil men do not understand judgment, But those who seek the Lord shall understand it in everything.
28.6: A poor man walking in the truth is better than a rich liar.
28.7: A wise son keeps the law, But he who cherishes luxurydishonors his father.
28.8: He who increases his wealth with usury and unjust gains Gathers it for him who shows mercy to the poor.
28.9: He who turns away his ear so as not to hear the law, He also makes his prayer repulsive.
28.10: He who leads upright men astray in an evil way, He shall fall into destruction;
28.11: And lawless men shall pass by good things, But they shall not enter into them.
28.12: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, But a poor man shall disapprove of his thoughts.
28.13: Great glory arises because of the help of the righteous, But in places of the ungodly, men are conquered.
28.14: He who hides his own ungodliness shall not prosper, But he who leads his own rebuttal shall be loved.
28.15: Blessed is the man who shall be discreet in all things because of godly fear, But the man who hardens his heart shall fall into evils.
28.16: A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf Is he who, being poor, tyrannizes over poor people.
28.17: A king in need of revenues is a great oppressor, But he who hates unrighteousness shall live a long time.
28.18: He who becomes surety for a man charged with murder Shall be a fugitive and unsafe.
28.19: Instruct your son, and he shall love you; And he shall give honor to your soul, Lest he follow a lawless people.
28.20: He who walks righteously shall be helped, But he who walks in crooked ways shall be entangled therein.
28.21: He who works his own land shall be satisfied with bread, But he who pursues leisure shall be filled with poverty.
28.22: A trustworthy man shall be blessed in many things, But an evil man shall not go unpunished.
28.23: He who does not respect righteous people is not good; Such a man will sell another for a morsel of bread.
28.24: An envious man hastens to be rich, But does not know that a merciful man shall have the mastery over him.
28.25: He who reproves a m an's ways Shall have more grace than he who flatters him.
28.26: He who casts off his father or mother and thinks he does not sin, He is the accomplice of an ungodly man.
28.27: A greedy man judges rashly, But he who trusts in the Lord shall be careful.
28.28: He who trusts in an arrogant heart, such a man is without discernment, But he who walks in wisdom, such a man shall be saved.
28.29: He who gives to the poor shall not be in want, But he who turns away his eye from them shall be in much distress.
28.30: The righteous lament in the places of the ungodly, But in their destruction the righteous shall be increased.

29.1: The Wise and the Unwise A reproving man is better than an obstinate man, For when the latter is suddenly consumed, there shall be no remedy.
29.2: When the righteous are praised, the people shall rejoice, But when the ungodly rule, men lament.
29.3: When a man loves wisdom, his father rejoices, But he who keeps prostitutes shall destroy his wealth.
29.4: A righteous king will establish a country, But a lawless man razes it to the ground.
29.5: He who prepares a net for the presence of his own friend Casts it around his own feet.
29.6: It is a great snare to a man when he sins, But a righteous man shall be in joy and gladness.
29.7: A righteous man understands how to judge on behalf of the poor, But the ungodly man will not consider such knowledge; For he has no understanding heart for a poor man.
29.8: Pestilent men burn down a city, But wise men turn away wrath.
29.9: A wise man judges people fairly, But when a worthless man is angry, he laughs at them, and does not fear.
29.10: Blood thirsty men will hate a holy man, But the upright will seek his soul.
29.11: A man without discernment brings forth his whole mind, But a wise man distributes his in part.
29.12: When a king obeys an unrighteous word, All those under him are lawless.
29.13: When a creditor and a debtor meet with one another, The Lord watches both of them.
29.14: When a king judges the poor truly, His throne shall be established as a testimony.
29.15: Blows and reproofs give wisdom, But a child who goes astray sham es his parents.
29.16: When the ungodly are many, there are many sins, But when they fall, the righteous are fearful.
29.17: Instruct your son, and he shall give you rest, And he will delight your soul.
29.18: There shall be no interpreter of the law for a lawless nation, But he who guards the law is very blessed.
29.19: A stubborn servant will not be instructed by words, For even if he understands them, he will not obey.
29.20: If you see a man hasty in words, Know a man without discernment has more hope than he.
29.21: He who lives luxuriously from childhood shall be a servant, And in the end, he shall cause him self pain.
29.22: An angry man digs up strife, But a furious man digs up sins.
29.23: Arrogance humbles a man, But the Lord supports the hum ble-m inded with glory.
29.24: He who takes part with a thief hates his own soul, And if, when an oath is set forth, those who hear it do not report it,
29.25: They are tripped up, because they fear and stand in awe of men; But he who trusts in the Lord will rejoice.
29.26: Ungodliness causes a man to stumble, But he who trusts in the Master shall be saved.
29.27: Many serve in the presence of leaders, But righteousness comes to a man from the Lord.
29.28: An abomination to the righteous is an unrighteous man, And the upright way is an abomination to the lawless.

30.1: My son, fear my words, A Father's Wisdom And when you receive them, repent; The man says these things to those who believe in God, then I cease speaking;
30.2: For I am the most lacking of all men in discernment, And the discernment of men is not in me;
30.3: God gives me wisdom, And I know holy things.
30.4: Who ascends into heaven and descends? Who gathers the winds in His bosom? Who wraps up the water in a garment? Who rules over all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His children, That you might acknowledge it?
30.5: All the words of God are tried in fire, And He defends those who fear Him.
30.6: Do not add to His words, That He might not reprove you, and you become a liar.
30.7: Two things I ask from You: Do not take away grace from me before I die;
30.8: Make a vain word and a lie be far from me; But give me neither riches nor poverty, And appoint what is necessary and sufficient for me;
30.9: Lest being full, I become a liar and say, “Who sees me?” Or being poor, I steal, and swear by the name of God.
30.10: Do not deliver a servant into the hands of his master, Lest he curse you, and you be destroyed.
30.11: An evil offspring curses his father And does not bless his mother.
30.12: An evil offspring judges himself righteous, But is not washed from his uncleanness.
30.13: An evil offspring has haughty eyes And exalts himself with his eyelids;
30.14: An evil offspring has teeth like swords And molars like knives, so as to destroy
30.15: And to devour the poor from the earth, And their needy from among men. Lessons from the Animals
30.16: The leech had three dearly loved daughters, And these three did not satisfy her, And the fourth did not satisfy her, for her to say, “It is enough.”
30.17: Hades and the love of a woman And Tartarus and the earth not satisfied with water, And water and fire will not say, “It is enough.”
30.18: The eye that mocks his father and dishonors the old age of his mother, Let the ravens of the valleys pick it out, And the young eagles devour it.
30.19: Now there are three things I cannot understand, And a fourth I do not know:
30.20: The track of a flying eagle, And the ways of a serpent upon a rock,
30.21: And the paths of a ship passing through the sea, And the ways of a man in his youth.
30.22: Such is the way of an adulterous woman, Who, when she commits adultery, washes herself and says she did nothing wrong.
30.23: The earth is shaken by three things, And is unable to bear a fourth:
30.24: If a servant reigns, Or a man without discernment is satiated with food,
30.25: Or if a maidservant casts out her own mistress, Or a hateful woman marries a good man.
30.26: Now there are four very small things upon earth, But these are wiser than the wise:
30.27: The ants, which are not strong, Yet they prepare provisions in the summer;
30.28: The rabbits, which are not a strong tribe, Yet they make their own homes in the rocks;
30.29: The locust, which is without a king, Yet he marches out as one commanded in an orderly manner.
30.30: And the spotted lizard, which supports himself with his hands and is easily caught, Yet he dwells in the fortresses of kings.
30.31: There are three things which walk easily, And a fourth that strides well:
30.32: The cub of a lion, stronger than other animals And does not turn away, neither fears any animal;
30.33: A cock, walking about boldly among the hens; A he-goat, leading a flock; And a king, speaking publicly to the people.
30.34: If you abandon yourself to merriment And stretch forth your hand with contention, you will be dishonored.
30.35: Churn milk, and it will become butter; And if you squeeze som eone's nose, blood will come out; And if you draw out words, condem nations and contentions will emerge.

31.1: My words were spoken by God, The oracular response of a king, whom his mother instructed. A Mother's Wisdom
31.2: “What, my child, will you keep? What? The words of God.” My firstborn son, I say to you, “What, the child of my womb? What, the child of my vows?”
31.3: Do not give your wealth to women, Nor your heart or life to remorse.
31.4: Do all things with counsel; Drink wine with counsel; Princes are prone to anger, but let them not drink wine,
31.5: Lest while they drink, they forget wisdom, And be unable to judge the weak uprightly.
31.6: Give strong drink to those in sorrow, And wine to drink for those in pain,
31.7: So they may forget their poverty And no longer remember their grief.
31.8: Open your mouth for the word of God, And judge all men fairly;
31.9: Open your mouth and judge righteously, And plead the cause of the poor and helpless. A Virtuous Wife
31.10: Who will find a courageous wife? For such a one is more valuable than precious stones.
31.11: The heart of her husband trusts in her; She will not be at a loss for fine spoils, For she provides good things for her husband all her life.
31.12: She weaves wool and linen cloth And is productive with her hands.
31.13: She is like a ship trading afar off, So she procures her livelihood.
31.14: She also rises before dawn And gives food to her household, And appoints tasks for her maid servants.
31.15: Seeing a farm, she buy sit, And from the fruits of her hands she plants her plot of land.
31.16: Strongly girding her loins, She strengthens her arms for work.
31.17: She experiences work as a good thing, And her lamp is not quenched all night.
31.18: She extends her arms to do profitable things, And she applies her hands to the spindle.
31.19: She opens her hands to the poor And reaches out with her fruit to the needy.
31.20: Her husband is not anxious about those at home When he spends a long time elsewhere, For all her household are clothed.
31.21: She makes a double upper garment for her husband And garments of fine linen and purple for herself.
31.22: Her husband is respected at the gates And when he sits in council with the elders who inhabit the land.
31.23: She makes and sells fine linens And girdles to the Canaanites.
31.24: She opens her mouth carefully and lawfully And controls her tongue.
31.25: She clothes herself with strength and dignity And rejoices in the last day s.
31.26: She runs her household carefully, And she does not eat the bread of idleness.
31.27: She opens her mouth wisely and lawfully, And her charity raises her children, and they become rich, And her husband praises her,
31.28: “Many daughters acquire riches; many do mighty things, But you excel and surpass all.”
31.29: Desires to please are deceitful, and the beauty of a wife is vain; For a wise wife is blessed, And let her in fear praise the Lord.
31.30: Give to her from the fruits of her hands, And let her husband praise her at the gates.
